_form: THE PUBLIC VOCABULARY OF THE FORMATS THIS CLIENT IMPLEMENTS -- the dressing manifest's fields the loader exposes, the pin file's keys, and the fold's row and state keys. It is the ALLOW side of §25 backlog 741's leak guard: a name here is one the client must be able to write, because the client implements a format that names it. It is NOT a list of names that are secret, and it is not the guard's forbidden set -- that set is derived from the fetched artefacts and committed as digests in tests/forbidden_names.json, with no plaintext anywhere.
_why_this_file_exists_at_all: 741's guard derives its forbidden set from the fetched manifest's keys and leaf string values. Some of those names are ALSO the vocabulary of formats this client reads and writes: a loader that reads the manifest's era starts must name that field, and a pin file class that serialises the format's top-level keys must name those. Without an allow side the guard would refuse the client for implementing the contract it exists to implement. The allow side had to be DERIVED rather than typed, for the reason 741 removes the typed forbidden list in the first place -- a hand-kept list of eight names did not notice four newer ones -- so it is derived from this file and from contract/schema.json, and this file holds only names that are already public.
_what_an_entry_asserts: that the name belongs to a format this client implements, and is already public in the ruling or the schema the `why` names. An entry is NOT a judgement that the name is harmless: it is a claim about where the name comes from, which a reader can check against the citation. Decision 973's question is whether the SIMULATION's own vocabulary reaches this tree; a format the client implements is this tree's business by construction.
_the_rule_this_file_is_the_exception_to: a derived name is forbidden when it is compound snake_case -- six characters or more, carrying an underscore, with two or more segments. Measured at the landing: 52 of the manifest's 293 derived names pass that rule, and the rule cuts the collisions with this client's own 70 source files from 45 to 7. The rule drops ordinary words that appear in comment prose (`height` on 105 lines, `lattice` on 121, `nodata`, `derived`, `centres`, `bounds`, `footprint`) and keeps compound field names, which is the shape a leaked simulation name actually has. The seven that remain are this file's entries plus the reasoned allowance in tests/forbidden_names.json.

manifest_fields_the_loader_exposes.era_starts: the eras and their first years. `DressingLoad.era_starts()` is the method and the manifest key it reads; the slider's ticks are derived from it and from no second set of years (decision 2129 (c), owner ruling 2059 Q3). The client cannot read this field without naming it.
manifest_fields_the_loader_exposes.lattice: the patch lattice's digest, which the client checks against the centres file's own (§25 backlog 732). Below the rule's six-character floor, so it is listed for completeness rather than need.

pin_file_keys._public_by: decision 2075 and §22.8.9 -- the emission format is this client's half of the round trip, and src/dressing/pin_file.gd validates against it.
pin_file_keys.ruled_by: a top-level key of the format.
pin_file_keys.base_dressing: a top-level key: the dressing a pin file's author looked at (§22.8.9's name for it).
pin_file_keys.schedule_plan_digest: a top-level key, renamed by decision 2128 (ii) from the name it replaced. Both the current name and the refusal of the old one are the format's.
pin_file_keys.schedule_content_digest: THE NAME THAT ONE REPLACED, and it is here because it is load-bearing rather than historical: tools/rewrite_pins.py searches an emitted file for this literal in order to REFUSE it (decision 2128 (ii), §25 backlog 726), and tests/run_headless.gd asserts that refusal. A tool that cannot write the name it rejects cannot reject it. Removing the literal would not remove a leak; it would remove a check.
pin_file_keys.authored_by: required on every pin of every kind, and refused on the file itself.
pin_file_keys.pin_id: a pin's identifier, which the explorer draws and the edit list keys on.

fold_keys._public_by: §25 backlog 730's fold format, which the client folds to and compares against the committed reference.
fold_keys.density_per_km2: a state key carried forward by the fold.

percept_fixture_keys._what: A SECOND FORMAT'S VOCABULARY, not a coincidence. These are fields of this client's own percept fixture -- a format that predates any dressing work, is declared in this repository's own committed PINs and is carried in its own committed artefacts. One of them happens to be spelled like a dressing-manifest key; the spelling is shared and the provenance is not.
percept_fixture_keys._why_it_cannot_simply_be_rewritten: the artefact data carrying it is PINNED BY DIGEST. assets/fixture/fixture_client.json and assets/contours/contours_deepest_winter_band_snowpack_swe.json each hold the field under `/run/`, and editing a byte of either breaks the PIN that claims its content digest. Exempting pinned artefact data from the scan was considered and rejected: that silences a whole class of files, future artefacts included, to avoid naming one field.
percept_fixture_keys.master_seed: the percept fixture run's seed, 20260820. DECLARED at assets/fixture/PIN:11 as that PIN's own field, and carried under `/run/` in assets/fixture/fixture_client.json and assets/contours/contours_deepest_winter_band_snowpack_swe.json. It was also an envelope field of contract/schema.json before v2.0 removed it (see src/contract/schema_loader.gd's version note), so it is public in this tree's own contract history as well as in its data.

client_own_names_colliding_by_coincidenc._what: NOT format vocabulary, and the only group here that is not. A name in this group is one THIS CLIENT independently chose for its OWN data, which happens to be spelled the same as a key in the simulation's manifest. No contract file will ever list it, because it is not part of any shared format; and it is not a leak, because nothing about it came from the simulation. The guard cannot tell the difference, so the difference is recorded here, by name, with where it is used -- counted and few, so that a second one has to be ruled rather than appended.
client_own_names_colliding_by_coincidenc._the_count_is_the_control: one entry, as ruled. A group that grew quietly would become the typed allow list this whole arrangement exists to avoid, so `tools/recut_forbidden.py --selftest` asserts the count and the gate reports it. Raising it is a decision, not an edit.
client_own_names_colliding_by_coincidenc.speed_m_s: the client's own output field, written by src/bench/flight_trace.gd:327 (a pose-derived speed per frame) and src/transducer/debug_player.gd:82 (a playback step's speed). Both predate any dressing work and neither reads the manifest. The manifest also happens to carry a `speed_m_s` key; the collision is the word, not the provenance.

session_file_keys._public_by: decision 2149 (1) and owner ruling 2150 -- DA-11's play loop. The session directory's SCHEMAS cross into this tree as field names with no value, and a client cannot read a field it may not name. Added by §25 backlog 752, one entry per name, BY THE ROW THAT FIRST NAMES IT IN CODE and never by pasting the guard's output.
session_file_keys._what_an_entry_here_asserts: that the name is a field of the session format this client reads or writes -- `session.json`, `year_<Y>/stats.json`, `year_<Y>/fold.json`, `commands/*.json` and their answers under `commands/done/` -- and that a source file in this tree names it because it reads or writes that field. A NAME THE CLIENT DOES NOT READ IS NOT HERE, which is the whole discipline: `session.json`'s `admissibility` block is declared in the schema and read past without naming one inner field, and `at_the_cap`'s rows carry a `schedule_row` key that §25 backlog 741 forbids EXPLICITLY and permanently, so the panel reads those rows by `kind`, `type` and `tiles` and never names it. Decision 2149 (1) puts the schemas in this tree; it does not put every field of them in this client's source.
session_file_keys._the_teeth_and_they_are_real: THESE NAMES ARE ALSO DERIVED. The committed synthetic session under `tests/session_fixture/recorded/` is one of the guard's derivation sources, so every name below is read out of a file the guard walks. An entry deleted from here therefore does not merely lose a comment: the name falls out of the allow side, the derivation puts its digest in the forbidden set, and `tools/recut_forbidden.py` goes red naming the departure before anything else runs -- and after a re-cut the scan refuses the source file that names it. That is what makes `by ruling` a mechanism rather than an intention, and `tests/run_headless.gd` proves it by dropping one name from the allow side and asserting the derived set grows by exactly that digest.
session_file_keys.dressing_id: the id of the dressing the session plays, under which an accepted city replaces it in place.
session_file_keys.base_dressing_id: the committed dressing the session was opened against. The explorer keys its era ticks on it and refuses by id when it is not the dressing this clone fetched (§25 backlog 753).
session_file_keys.pins_sha256: the session's working pin file's sha256. The fold binding compares a fold's own against the shas this session has had, which is what catches a year drawn from a fold written before the last placement.
session_file_keys.start_pins: the pin file the session opened over, as `{path, sha256}`. Its sha is the first the session ever had, and therefore the first member of the set a fold may legitimately carry.
session_file_keys.last_step_s: the wall cost of the last advance, shown so the owner knows what a step costs before asking for another.
session_file_keys.code_state: NAMED ONLY IN ORDER TO DROP IT. A map of the generator's `*.py` files to their digests, i.e. a listing of the private tree's layout, which decision 973 makes not this tree's to republish. The reader deletes it at load so it cannot reach a screen, a log line or a crash dump.
session_file_keys.generator_commit: NAMED ONLY IN ORDER TO DROP IT, for the same reason -- a private-repo commit sha. The reader deletes it at load and nothing draws it.
session_file_keys.built_tiles: the ledger's built-tile count. THE PANEL'S COUNT IS THIS ONE (§25 backlog 750's rule), with the fold's own count beside it and their agreement stated.
session_file_keys.built_km2: the ledger's built area, shown against the bound's cap.
session_file_keys.quota_carried: the ledger's quota carried by class.
session_file_keys.at_the_cap: the ledger's at-the-cap rows. Read by `kind`, `type` and `tiles` only -- see `_what_an_entry_here_asserts`.
session_file_keys.irrigated_take_km2: the fabric's irrigated land built over.
session_file_keys.capacity_less_occupancy: §22.7's D1 as the running line `capacity - occupancy >= 0`, which decision 2149 (4) asks the panel to show every year.
session_file_keys.ledger_tiles: the ledger's count as the `built` block restates it, which is the field the panel actually reads.
session_file_keys.cap_tiles: the bound's built-tile cap, the count's denominator.
session_file_keys.feature_in_window: a named part of §25 backlog 750's rule, shown so that the count's parts are legible rather than a single number the owner must trust.
session_file_keys.feature_outside: the same rule's excluded part -- a structure seated off the window.
session_file_keys.quotas_tiles: the demand line's next-year quotas by class, in tiles.
session_file_keys.quotas_note: the generator's own note on what the quotas precede. DRAWN AS DATA READ AT RUNTIME, never copied into a source file -- the same standing as the palette's class names, which reach the viewer from the fetched file and are not re-declared (decision 2129 (b)).
session_file_keys.strata_note: likewise: the generator's note that a stratum's tile figure is a BOUND, because its tiles depend on a saturation only the step knows (§25 backlog 749's construal of decision 2149 (4)).
session_file_keys.tiles_at_least: a stratum's tile lower bound, labelled as a bound for the reason `strata_note` gives.
session_file_keys.serviceable_open_tiles: the serviceable open tiles standing, which the owner places against.
session_file_keys.enclosed_note: the generator's note on when the enclosed count was last read -- a figure whose meaning depends on it, so showing the number without the note would mislead.
session_file_keys.holds_releasing: the holds releasing in the demand year.
session_file_keys.arc_start: the arc's first year, which is the floor a rewind is priced against.
session_file_keys.to_year: `rewind`'s target year. THIS ONE THE CLIENT WRITES rather than reads: the command file is the client's half of the format.
session_file_keys.year_issued: the year a command was issued at, as the answer reports it back.
session_file_keys.cost_s: a priced rewind's or removal's cost in seconds, shown while the session works, since a rewind can cost a whole build.

_not_in_here_on_purpose.the_session_schemas: NO LONGER PENDING, AND THE PARAGRAPH IS KEPT BECAUSE IT PREDICTED CORRECTLY. It stood here from §25 backlog 741's landing, saying that decision 2149 (1)'s session field names would cross AFTER this guard, that several were manifest keys passing the rule, and that the row making them public would have to add them WITH THEIR REASON or go red. That row was §25 backlog 752 and it did: they are in `session_file_keys` above. What the prediction got wrong is the SIZE -- it said `several`, and 752's dispatch named two (`built_tiles`, `built_km2`); the measured answer is about thirty-three, because `stats.json` splices the whole ledger and fabric records in verbatim and nests the whole demand line. A reader estimating this work from either figure would have been wrong by more than an order of magnitude, which is why the count was measured against `tools/play_dressing.py` before a line was written rather than taken from the brief.
_not_in_here_on_purpose.the_bid_fields: owner ruling 2150 keeps the generator's bid maps out of the first version, so their names are not this tree's and are not here.
_not_in_here_on_purpose.anything_merely_convenient: a name that collides because this client independently chose the same word for its own data is NOT format vocabulary, and it is kept in its own group above rather than mixed in with the formats'. There is exactly one, with its two call sites; the groups are separate so that a reader can see at a glance how much of the allow side is a contract and how much is a coincidence.
